summary: This paper constructs TENSOR-SPECTRUM-CONN-CERT-1.0, an exact-Z/Q, zero-float machine-checked verification suite for the asymptotic spectrum of tensors, building upon Vrana and Zuiddam's path-connectedness theorem. All 20 core theorems are verified constructively in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry, zero axioms, and paired with 16 SHA-256 indexed exact rational certificates audited by 62 adversarial pytest checks. Key contributions include exact flattening-rank semiring homomorphisms, root-free simplex-edge interpolation intervals, an explicit 8-entry Z[epsilon] border-rank-2 witness for W3 demonstrating strict cube separation (27/4 < 8) and exponential tensor-power amplification, and exact graph asymptotic spectrum sandwiches for C5 and C7 via root-free Chebyshev polynomial root brackets. The work establishes exemplary standards for formal mathematics and exact rational scientific computing.
strengths: Complete constructive formalization in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry, zero axioms, and zero Classical.choice, establishing absolute logical soundness for all 20 core asymptotic tensor spectrum theorems.
Rigorous exact-Z/Q Python verification engine implementing rational Gaussian elimination and 16 SHA-256 indexed certificates validated across 62 adversarial pytest test cases.
First explicit root-free algebraic certification of W3 border rank 2 and strict spectral gap separation (27/4 < 8) along with exponential tensor-power amplification.
Pioneering exact Chebyshev polynomial root isolation via the Intermediate Value Theorem for C7 Lovász-theta graph capacity bounds without floating-point approximations.
weaknesses: The general path-connectedness theorem of Vrana and Zuiddam relies on advanced symmetric-group representation theory that is imported as an external cited lemma rather than re-proved within Lean.
